source_text: Sicut autem hic semen maledictum, sic alibi equidem, ubi maior est lectionis auctoritas, semen dicitur benedictum. Loquens enim de Israelitis Isaias propheta: Aedificabunt, inquit, domus, et ipsi inhabitabunt; pastinabunt vineas, et ipsi manducabunt fructus earum; non aedificabunt, et alii habitabunt; et non pastinabunt, et alii manducabunt. Secundum enim dies ligni vitae, erunt dies populi mei; opera labiorum eorum perseverant; electi mei non laborabunt in vacuum, nec filios procreabunt in maledicto, quia semen benedictum a Deo est [n215] .
pass_a_gloss: But as here a cursed seed, so elsewhere indeed, where the authority of the reading is greater, a seed is called blessed. For speaking of the Israelites Isaiah the prophet: They will build houses, he says, and they themselves will inhabit; they will plant vineyards, and they themselves will eat their fruits; they will not build, and others inhabit; and they will not plant, and others eat. For according to the days of the tree of life will be the days of my people; the works of their lips persevere; my elect will not labor in vain, nor will they beget sons in a curse, because it is a seed blessed by God.

lemmas.lexica: LS malum; Blaise malum naturale vs malum voluntatis
LS opus; Blaise God's works vs devil's

pass_b_english: Just as the seed is called cursed here, elsewhere, in a reading of greater authority, it is called blessed. For the prophet Isaiah says of the Israelites: “They will build houses and inhabit them themselves; they will plant vineyards and eat their fruit themselves. They will not build for others to inhabit, or plant for others to eat. For the days of my people will be like the days of the tree of life. The works of their lips endure. My chosen ones will not labor in vain or beget children under a curse, because they are seed blessed by God” (Isaiah 65:21–23).

choices.why: Seed is God's work in generation; Julian refuses to make semen a vehicle of natural evil.
rejected: original sin (later system as default gloss)
